title: Scotch stitch
subtitle: Five diagonal stitches forming a square block on canvas
excerpt: Scotch stitch builds square blocks across the canvas, each made from five diagonal stitches increasing then decreasing in length. The blocks create a raised, textured surface and cover the canvas in a satisfying rhythm.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), canvaswork chapter. Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), Scotch stitch entry. Weldon's Practical Needlework, canvaswork series.

glossaryTerms.definition: Five diagonal stitches worked over one, two, three, two, and one canvas intersection in sequence. The five stitches form a square block. The blocks tile the canvas in a diagonal grid.

heroPrompt: Scotch stitch blocks on 13-count canvas in warm tan wool, showing the raised square blocks in a diagonal grid, natural light.

content.text: Scotch stitch works five diagonal stitches in a sequence: over one canvas intersection, over two, over three, over two, over one. The five stitches form a neat square block, three holes wide and three holes tall. The blocks tile the canvas with a diagonal grid pattern.
The raised centre stitch gives the surface a slight woven texture.
covers canvas faster than tent stitch and is useful for geometric borders, backgrounds, and any area where a bold texture is wanted.

items.label: Canvas
items.value: 13-count mono canvas on a scroll frame

items.label: Thread
items.value: One strand of Persian wool, or two strands of tapestry wool

content.text: Mark a three-by-three square area of canvas (nine holes by nine holes, giving one block with a border). Bring the needle up at the lower left of the block.

Stitch 1: one diagonal over one intersection. Stitch 2: one diagonal over two intersections, starting one hole lower and one to the right. Stitch 3: one diagonal over three intersections. Stitch 4: over two intersections. Stitch 5: over one intersection. The five stitches fill the three-by-three block.
Move to the next block three holes to the right. Repeat the five-stitch sequence.
At the end of the row, begin the second row three holes below the first. Offset the blocks so the grid aligns.

A single row of tent stitch between the blocks, in a second colour, outlines each block and makes the grid more defined. This version is sometimes called chequered Scotch stitch. Work all the blocks first, then fill the single-hole gaps between them with tent stitch in the second colour.

items.symptom: Long centre stitch standing proud of the block
items.cause: The three-intersection stitch needs slightly less pull than the shorter stitches on either side.
items.fix: Keep all five stitches in one block at the same gentle tension. The centre stitch will appear slightly raised, which is normal and desirable.
Each block occupies exactly three canvas holes in both directions. Count the starting hole before placing the first stitch of each block.
